Subject: Training on customer data — opt-out

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier today. A couple of follow-ups from our security/privacy team: does Redwood ever use customer request/response data (including PII) to improve or train models? If so, can you describe the retention period, logging controls, and whether we can opt our traffic out of any training or model-improvement pipelines?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@acmefin.com) who will need any formal opt-out acknowledgement for contract records.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Training on customer data — opt-out

Hi Alex —

Great question, and thanks for flagging procurement. Short answer: by default, Redwood does not use customer data from production inference traffic to train public models. For clarity: 1) We do collect operational logs (request metadata, latency, error traces) for debugging and SLOs; 2) Customer request/response bodies are stored only as configured by the customer and can be disabled/shortened via logging controls; 3) For customers that opt-in, we may use anonymized, aggregated signals to improve product quality, but we require explicit customer consent for any training-on-customer-data workflows.

I've attached our standard training-opt-out form that provides a one-line opt-out confirmation we can sign and return. If you prefer, Stephanie (cc'd) from Security can provide the SOC2/controls excerpt and confirm the technical measures (retention windows, PII redaction hooks, and KV cache policies).

Next steps I suggest:
- Alex: review attached opt-out form and confirm the contact for signatures (procurement?).
- Procurement: if you need a DocuSign link or company legal name for the form, let us know.
- Stephanie: can you add the short controls summary for Alex?

I'll hold the opt-out in our system until we receive the signed acknowledgement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Training on customer data — opt-out confirmation

Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers below and confirmation of next steps.

1) Console setting & retention: Under Console > Settings > Data & Logging there is a toggle labeled "Store full request/response bodies" (default: ON for trial accounts, OFF for production by request). If enabled, retention is configurable from 7 to 90 days; default retention for production is 30 days. We can set your account to OFF and enforce a 0-day retention for request/response bodies if required (we would retain minimal operational metadata only).

2) Audit log on opt-out: Yes — when we flag an account as "Training Opt-Out: ENABLED" we generate an immutable audit event (timestamped) and export a signed acknowledgement PDF. The event is stored in the account's audit log and can be exported to your S3/GCS for archival.

Attached is the completed opt-out form. For your records: by signing, Redwood confirms it will not use AcmeFin production request/response content for any training or model improvement pipelines; only operational metadata (latency, error rates) will be used in aggregated/anonymous form. We will implement the opt-out within one business day of receiving the signed acknowledgement.

DocuSign link for signature: https://www.docusign.com/AAAA-ACME-OPT-OUT-123

Attachments: acmefin_training_opt_out_form.pdf

If procurement prefers, we can also email the signed PDF back and push the audit event into a shared S3 bucket.

Thanks — I'll follow up once the opt-out is in place.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acmefin_training_opt_out_form.pdf
